File the licence now in bulk and fly on release (about USD 1.8K, no slip, recommended), add a 60 set buffer on the same licence (about USD 3.9K, no slip), flux-test and reuse removed magnet sets where the CMM allows (about USD 2.4K, uncertain yield), or wait for the standard process (nil at a 30 day licence, USD 22K and 11 days at 45 days).

Filing now and flying on release is cheapest at about USD 1.8K of air freight. Waiting costs nothing if the licence takes 30 days but USD 22K if it takes 45, and the sets are sole source with no stock on hand.

In 2025 export licence processing for a dual-use sensor family stretched to five weeks (PRE-08). We covered two engines from Singapore distributor stock for USD 52K with 3 days of slip, but there is no distributor source for these magnets. The lesson we can use is to file licences per quarter in bulk rather than per consignment.
